audit_scope.description: EIP-7892 covers both EL (timestamp-based blob parameter activation, excess blob gas computation) and CL (epoch-based activation, P2P fork digest rotation). EIP-7883 covers EL state transition (ModExp precompile gas repricing). EIP-8123 covers JSON-RPC query interface (out-of-scope per bug bounty but modeled for completeness).

out_of_scope: JSON-RPC API (EIP-8123 eth_txGasLimitCap is out-of-scope per bug bounty)

in_scope: P2P Network (fork digest rotation, ENR updates)

judging.poc_requirement_note: All submissions (except informational) must include an executable coded proof of concept at the time of submission

engine_api.description: EL-CL communication via Engine API is authenticated using JWT and considered semi-trusted
engine_api.rationale: Co-located EL and CL clients communicate via authenticated Engine API (JWT). The Engine API is considered a trusted boundary, but data returned by EL may not be fully verified by CL in all cases (e.g., blob data from engine_getBlobsV2 is used without KZG verification). If the EL is compromised or buggy, corrupted data may be propagated to the network.
security_implications: Engine API is authenticated via JWT
Some data from EL may be used without full verification by CL
Compromised EL can affect CL behavior
engine_api.note: Vulnerabilities in Engine API implementation are in-scope, but attacks requiring a compromised local EL may be considered conditional or lower severity

local_validator.description: Local validator configuration is under operator control and considered semi-trusted
local_validator.rationale: Local validator configuration is under operator control. Misconfigured or manipulated validator settings could cause incorrect node behavior.
local_validator.note: Configuration issues requiring operator error are typically out-of-scope

p2p_peers.description: P2P network peers are unauthenticated and considered untrusted
p2p_peers.rationale: P2P network peers are unauthenticated. Any node can join the network and send arbitrary protocol messages. All P2P input must be fully validated.
p2p_peers.note: Vulnerabilities exploitable via P2P network are high priority for bug bounty

Critical.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Exploit an EIP/specification or client bug to easily create an infinite amount of ETH which is finalized by the network
Take down the entire network by sending a single malicious on-chain transaction that ends up crashing all clients
Critical.impact: Entire network (>50% validators or all clients)
Critical.attack_vector: Single malicious on-chain transaction or network packet

High.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Trivially cause network splits affecting more than 33% of the network
Bring down more than 33% of the network by sending a single network packet or an on-chain transaction
High.attack_vector: Single network packet or on-chain transaction

Medium.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Trivially cause network splits affecting more than 5% of the network
Bring down more than 5% of the network by sending a single network packet or an on-chain transaction
Medium.impact: More than 5% of the network (or >1% of validators for slashing)
Medium.attack_vector: Single network packet or on-chain transaction

Low.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Trivially cause network splits affecting at least 0.01% of the network
Bring down more than 0.01% of the network by sending a single network packet or an on-chain transaction
Low.attack_vector: Single network packet or on-chain transaction

Informational.criteria: Observations or recommendations regarding code quality, maintainability, or system architecture that do not present a direct security risk
Informational.validity_requirement: Only applicable if the team decides to implement a change based on the report
notes: Informational issues are valid if they don't lead to a sufficient impact to count as Low or higher and are valuable enough for the client that they decided to implement the change in the code
Issues related to parts under the 'Out of scope' section will not be considered valid
Informational issues won't have duplicates, and only the first one is valid
They also don't qualify for the 1st and 2nd week multipliers, as they apply only to issues in the main pot

out_of_scope_reasons.EIP-8123 (eth_txGasLimitCap): This EIP defines a JSON-RPC method. JSON-RPC API is explicitly out-of-scope per Ethereum Bug Bounty. Additionally, EIP-8123 is not listed in the Fusaka EIP set.

el_attack_vectors.threat: Submit transactions that exploit ModExp gas repricing edge cases (EIP-7883) or crafted calldata to the ModExp precompile that is underpriced relative to computation cost.
Send blocks with manipulated blob gas parameters during BPO fork transition (EIP-7892), potentially causing validation disagreements between nodes with different blob schedule configurations.

cl_attack_vectors.threat: Exploit fork digest rotation during BPO fork activation (EIP-7892) to partition the network by subscribing to old/new gossip topics selectively.
Propose blocks at BPO fork boundary with inconsistent blob parameters between EL and CL, exploiting potential misalignment in activation timing.

misclassified_entities.reason: EXT-RPC-NODE represents the local Ethereum node itself responding to RPC queries. This is an internal component, not an external entity. The node computing min(protocolCap, policyCap) is internal processing.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via Gossip/ENR (EIP-7892)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P gossip topics and ENR discovery (fork digest rotation at BPO fork activation)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated. During BPO fork activation, peers advertise fork digests via ENR and subscribe to gossip topics. Malicious peers could exploit the fork digest transition to cause topic fragmentation or eclipse attacks.

trusted_external_entities.name: EVM Caller via On-chain Transaction (EIP-7883)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any EOA or contract can invoke the ModExp precompile with arbitrary input data. The caller controls base_length, modulus_length, exponent_length, and all operand values. Input is fully untrusted.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet User via JSON-RPC (EIP-8123)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: User interacting with wallet to query gas cap. OUT OF SCOPE per bug bounty (JSON-RPC API is explicitly excluded). Included for completeness only.
trusted_external_entities.bug_bounty_note: OUT_OF_SCOPE - JSON-RPC API vulnerabilities are explicitly excluded from the Ethereum Bug Bounty program.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via Block Propagation (EIP-7892)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P block propagation containing blob gas fields (excess_blob_gas, blob_gas_used)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers propagate blocks whose blob gas fields must be validated against the active blob schedule. Incorrect validation during BPO fork transition could lead to consensus splits.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P gossip topic subscription and ENR discovery
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Nodes must validate that peer ENR fork digests match expected values for the current and next fork. Gossip messages on old fork digest topics must be rejected after fork activation grace period. Fork digest computation must be deterministic across all clients.

Gas cost must accurately reflect computational cost for all input combinations. The new formula (EIP-7883) must prevent underpriced inputs that could cause disproportionate CPU usage. Input parsing must handle malformed calldata safely. The minimum gas floor of 500 must be enforced.
OUT OF SCOPE per bug bounty. For completeness: node must return accurate cap values; null handling must be correct; no information leakage beyond intended gas cap data.

Block validation must use the correct blob schedule parameters for the block's timestamp. During BPO fork transition, the exact activation boundary must be handled consistently. Excess blob gas calculation must use the updated formula with blob_schedule.target instead of hardcoded TARGET_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK. Mismatch between EL and CL blob parameter activation must be detected or prevented.

notes: EXT-USER-WALLET and its boundary edge are OUT OF SCOPE per bug bounty but included for model completeness.
EIP-8123 (source spec_a748a1ed13202138e24a989c1840a06b4160e42e.json) is not listed in the Fusaka EIP set and its JSON-RPC interface is out-of-scope.

EIP-7892 subgraphs for blob gas computation and fork activation have no external entities in the original model; external entities were inferred from archetypal attack vectors (P2P block propagation).
